title: The house and its repairs
description: Say what has broken and get it fixed.

explanation.summary: Things in a house break, and then somebody comes and fixes them. Telling the story of a repair needs the preterite, because every step of it is a finished action with a clear time in the past.

sections.heading: The things that break
sections.body: A house is a set of parts and each one can fail. El grifo gotea, la tubería está rota, el techo tiene una gotera, el suelo está mojado. The word for the problem itself is la avería: hay una avería en la caldera y no hay agua caliente.

examples.es: El grifo de la cocina pierde agua.
Hay una gotera en el techo del salón.
examples.en: There is a leak in the ceiling of the living room.

sections.heading: Telling the story of a repair
sections.body: When you tell somebody what happened, use the preterite. El grifo se rompió el martes. Llamé al fontanero. Vino a las tres y arregló la tubería en media hora. Each verb is a finished action, which is exactly what the preterite is for. If you want to say what was happening in the middle of it, use the imperfect: el fontanero arreglaba la tubería cuando llegué.

examples.es: Se rompió el grifo el martes por la mañana.
examples.en: The tap broke on Tuesday morning.

examples.es: El fontanero llegó antes de las tres.

sections.heading: Who does the work
sections.body: Un fontanero works with water: grifos, tuberías, heating, cisterns. Un electricista works with electricity: enchufes, lights, the meter. The general verbs are reparar and arreglar, and both take a thing as their object: hay que reparar la caldera, tenemos que arreglar la puerta.

examples.en: I have to repair the boiler.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: A repair is a chain of finished actions: se rompió el grifo, llamé al fontanero, lo arregló.

exercises.prompt: Pick the Spanish word for “the tap”.
exercises.note: Masculine: el grifo. The tap that gives the water.
Feminine: la tubería. The pipes inside the walls.
The preterite of romperse is se rompió.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: A repair is a chain of finished actions: se rompió el grifo, llamé al fontanero, lo arregló.

exercises.prompt: Pick the Spanish word for “the breakdown”.
exercises.note: Feminine: la avería. A fault, something that does not work.

exercises.prompt: ___ al fontanero porque no había agua.
exercises.translation: I called the plumber because there was no water
exercises.note: Llamar in the preterite is llamé; había is the imperfect of haber.

exercises.prompt: El fontanero ___ la gotera del techo.
exercises.translation: the plumber fixed the leak in the roof
exercises.note: Arreglar in the preterite is arregló.

exercises.prompt: La tubería ___ en el segundo piso.
exercises.translation: the pipe is broken on the second floor
exercises.note: Estar plus an adjective for a state that is true now.

exercises.translation: I need to repair the bathroom tap
